body: The radio test sheet says the signal dropped at the tower; the technician’s note asks the field crew to check power before changing equipment.
title: A signal sent for testing

body: Personal service note: dish three on tower two relayed moisture readings from the trial plots. The signal vanished during the night application, before any public emergency traffic.
title: Dish three carried plot readings

body: Torn meter log: near six gigahertz, power dipped as the spraying crew entered the eastern field. The station batteries were full and no storm was recorded.
title: Power dip during the field pass

body: Letter draft: ask headquarters to compare the Lexington receiver with two leaf samples. The samples carry the same gray film found inside the tower cabinet.
title: Test request with samples attached

body: Photograph back at the sun mark: the crop-weather receiver is lit, but its plot channel reads blank. The operator noted a chemical smell inside the cabinet.
title: Sun mark over the crop receiver

body: Technician’s notebook: the cross marks the receiver used for crop-weather telemetry. It failed whenever the treated field pump ran, then recovered after the pump stopped.
title: Cross placed over the test receiver
